reason: The load meter can establish what the radios draw before we plan their independent power.
expectation: The meter will measure the radio kit's power demand.

effect: The meter tested the batteries under load rather than measuring the radios; the tested pair can now support the power plan.
reaction: The automatic battery test was useful, though I had expected a radio measurement.
reason: The sightline scope should help establish a viable path for the rooftop radios.
expectation: The scope will help align or verify the radio link.

effect: The radios are installed and aligned along a clear sightline; they still need independent power.
reaction: The passing train made the sightline check feel concrete.
reason: The matched power boxes are the natural connection between the tested batteries and the radios.
expectation: The tested batteries and power boxes will form a suitable independent radio supply.

effect: The tested batteries now have matched local fuse protection and are ready to supply the radios.
reaction: The separate protection for each radio makes the power setup clearer.
reason: The protected reserves should supply the aligned rooftop radios independently of the uplink.
expectation: The radios will run on the protected battery supplies.

effect: The protected reserves cannot currently be combined with anything, so another preparation may be needed before powering the radios.
reaction: That was unexpected; the supplies seemed ready to connect.
reason: Inspecting the aligned radios should reveal what they currently need without guessing at the power sequence.
expectation: The inspection will show their available connection or preparation partners.

alternatives.reason: The reserves may need their charging equipment first, but the failed attempt suggests checking the radios instead.

effect: The controller established a private market-to-clinic radio route; the independent power arrangement still needs attention.
reaction: I hadn't expected the network connection to come before the power connection.
reason: The solar charging pair is the remaining power component, but the protected reserves previously had no available combination. Inspecting it should clarify the next step.
expectation: The inspection will identify where the solar chargers fit into the power setup.

effect: The solar chargers have no available partner yet, so they do not resolve the power sequence now.
reaction: That leaves their role unclear for the moment.
reason: The newly established radio link may now accept the protected reserves; they were unavailable before the link existed.
expectation: The protected reserves will power the established radio link.

alternatives.reason: I could check its available partners first, but the reserves are a plausible next connection.

effect: Both radios now run on protected reserves, with the old wall adapter disconnected; the solar chargers may now be usable.
reaction: Separating the wall adapter made the independence claim more convincing.
reason: The matched solar chargers can plausibly replenish the batteries powering the link.
expectation: The solar chargers will be added to the radio link's reserve power arrangement.

effect: The link now has solar charging connected for daylight, but the panels add no energy tonight.
reaction: The distinction between stored power tonight and charging tomorrow is useful.
reason: The local link is the central construction for the remaining power goal; inspecting it should reveal its next available operation.
expectation: The inspection will show what can be done with the completed power arrangement.

effect: The measured radio loads and tested battery capacities confirm coverage through the remaining night, with a margin and a scheduled recheck. The next goal is to reach Eli.
reaction: The load test makes the independence claim more credible.
reason: Moth is the available communication-capable device, so connecting it to the tested link is a plausible way to reach Eli.

choice.combine: Moth with source display and correction controls

expectation: Moth will use the local link to contact Eli at the clinic.

effect: Eli's reply confirms the clinic link works, completing the chapter; Tin Row's call suggests a possible next challenge in connecting networks.
reaction: Eli's noodle message was a satisfying, human confirmation of the technical work.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the operating radios against the batteries' measured capacity was most worthwhile: it turned an independence claim into a bounded overnight plan with a margin and a recheck.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the solar chargers yielded no available partner and did not clarify when they would become usable.

surprise.text: I expected the protected reserves to connect directly to the aligned radios, but the controller had to establish the local route first.

arbitrary.text: That required ordering felt somewhat arbitrary: the failed power connection gave no indication that the network route needed to be established first.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the practical link test was satisfying, and Tin Row's invitation raises a concrete question about how the networks can work together.
